clue.text: Criticised after openings of some courses cancelled

indicators.note: after places the criticism word behind the two opening letters
the openings of words are their first letters, here of some and courses

parts.note: first letter of some
first letter of courses
rapped means criticised sharply, as in rapped over the knuckles

explanation.surface: Someone is criticised after a few college courses are suddenly dropped from the timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans that were scrapped have been abandoned or called off, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Think company will have special appeal amongst spectators

indicators.note: amongst places the appeal word inside the spectators word

parts.note: the gate is the number of spectators at a sporting event
it is sex appeal or star quality, a special allure

explanation.surface: A firm reckons it will be attractive to the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To cogitate is to ponder or reflect deeply, a formal synonym of think.

clue.text: Soldier is repeatedly besetting the opposition

parts.note: a soldier ant is a caste of ant, so ant stands for soldier

indicators.note: besetting means surrounding, so the doubled word goes round the

parts.note: repeatedly means the word is is used a second time, giving it twice

explanation.surface: A soldier keeps surrounding the enemy forces.
explanation.definitionFit: An antithesis is a direct contrast or opposite, the opposing idea set against another.

clue.text: Source of sharp pain? Repeats "Ooh!" when stricken

indicators.note: stricken means struck down and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone keeps yelping Ooh after being hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers a definition by example: a pea shot from a tube stings anyone it hits.
explanation.definitionFit: A peashooter is a toy tube for blowing dried peas, whose hits give a sudden sting.

clue.text: Manor-house finally collapsed — son brought in workers in middle of week

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of collapsed
in places the workers-with-son piece inside the middle of week
the middle of week is its central pair of letters
brought in means the son letter goes inside the workers word

parts.note: men are workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: A country house fell down, and a son brought in labourers midweek to rebuild it.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is the land and house a lord of the manor kept for himself, so it means the manor estate.

clue.text: American composer is overlooking intro

indicators.note: overlooking the intro means ignoring the first letter of the word for is

parts.note: lives can mean is, exists

explanation.surface: An American composer is ignoring an introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Ives was an early twentieth-century American modernist composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was a pioneering American composer known for experimental orchestral works.

clue.text: Take charge of narrative, lifting a veil

parts.note: to man something is to staff and take charge of it

indicators.note: lifting means taking away, so the a is removed from the narrative word

parts.note: a tale is a narrative

explanation.surface: Someone takes control of a story, raising the bride's veil.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantle is a cloak, and figuratively anything that covers or conceals like a veil.

clue.text: Upset to a great degree in certain circumstances

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is greatly upset about certain circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a great degree' reads as one phrase; split it after great, and degree belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An aegrotat is a university degree granted to a student too ill to sit the final examinations.

clue.text: Imagine a lot of discontented feelings around slump

indicators.note: around says the trimmed feelings word wraps the slump word
a lot of means most but not all, so the final letter of the feelings word is dropped

parts.note: envies are feelings of discontent at others' good fortune
to sag is to slump or droop

explanation.surface: Picture someone so full of resentment that they slump under the weight of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To envisage something is to picture it in the mind, so it is a synonym of imagine.

clue.text: Surprised comment about label that's brought back name of detective writer

indicators.note: about says the exclamation goes round the label word

parts.note: aha is an exclamation of surprise or discovery

indicators.note: brought back means the label word is read in reverse

parts.note: a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A reader exclaims at a book label revealing the author of a crime novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The detective writer is Agatha Christie; the answer is her first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha is the forename of Agatha Christie, the best-known British writer of detective fiction.

clue.text: Target of nepotism? Measures one's time in office: short!

parts.note: steps are measures taken, as in taking steps
one's is read as I'S, I being one

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the office word is cut off

parts.note: a term is a period in office

explanation.surface: A minister takes measures, though their time in office is brief, while favouring relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Nepotism is favouring family, and the question mark admits that a stepsister is only one possible relative to favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism means favouring relatives, and a stepsister is a family member who might benefit from such favouritism.

clue.text: Has now left, but not before a bath

parts.note: has, moved into the past once someone has gone, becomes was

indicators.note: but not tells us to take the before word out of the phrase

parts.note: someone now left was here, so the phrase supplies here
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A guest has finally departed, though only after taking a bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A wash is a cleaning of the body, much as a bath is, so the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Invincible men to point out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Unbeatable men are being pointed out to us.
explanation.definitionFit: Something omnipotent is all-powerful, so it cannot be beaten or overcome.

clue.text: One writing US city book to miss something on letter once

parts.note: a pen is a thing that writes
NY is short for New York
to lack something is to miss it, be without it

explanation.surface: A writer from a US city regrets missing something in an old letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Penny Black of 1840 was the world's first adhesive postage stamp, issued in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Penny Black was the first postage stamp, stuck on Victorian envelopes and long since withdrawn.

clue.text: Attaining less than zero, therefore really angry?

indicators.note: attaining is read as reaching round, so the therefore word takes in the rest

parts.note: thus means therefore
under means less than
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A score of below zero would make anyone furious.
explanation.definitionFit: A thunderous look is a furious one, dark as a storm, and the question mark marks the figurative sense.

clue.text: Refuse to accept position? That shows stupidity

indicators.note: to accept means the refuse word takes in the position word

parts.note: to deny is to refuse
sit can mean position or posture, as in the sit of a garment

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to accept their position is showing foolishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Density is thickness, used informally of a person's slowness of mind or obtuseness.

clue.text: Daughter turned up recording a book — here's a sample?

indicators.note: in a down answer turned up means the letters are read bottom to top, in reverse

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A daughter arrives having recorded an audiobook, apparently a sample.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo tape is a sample recording made by a band to show off its music to labels.

clue.text: Remit of coroner's query initially unites different cases

indicators.note: cases means the rearranged letters encase the query letter
different signals that the letters of unites are made different, reordered
initially picks the first letter of query

explanation.surface: A coroner's query brings together various cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding an inquest into a death is the formal job a coroner is charged with, so it is that official's remit.

clue.text: Small model encapsulating Queen of the Stars?

indicators.note: encapsulating means the model word encloses the queen letters

parts.note: an ideal is a model to follow
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A small model of the Queen of the Stars, a celebrity figurine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal means relating to the stars, as in sidereal time measured by them.

clue.text: Feel gutted, less healthy, with no initial sign of life?

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: outer letters of Feel

indicators.note: with no initial means the first letter of the healthy word is dropped

parts.note: sicker means less healthy

explanation.surface: Someone feeling gutted and unwell shows no sign of life.
explanation.definitionFit: A flicker is a faint movement or glimmer, such as the first stir showing someone is alive.

clue.text: Big church, not English cathedral, hosting small troupe of musicians

indicators.note: not means the English letter is removed from the church word

parts.note: a minster is a large or important church

indicators.note: hosting means the cathedral word holds the small letter

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A large church, not an English cathedral, plays host to a little band of players.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is an English cathedral city near Cambridge; the cathedral is used in the wordplay despite the surface's 'not English'.
explanation.definitionFit: Minstrelsy is the art of minstrels, and also a group of minstrels, wandering musicians.

clue.text: Want larvae gutted for bait

parts.note: need means want

indicators.note: gutted means emptied, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: outer letters of larvae

explanation.surface: An angler needs larvae with their insides removed to use as bait.
explanation.walkthrough: Bait here is the verb, to tease or provoke, not the angler's lure.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to provoke or goad them, the same sense as baiting them.

clue.text: Old-fashioned person repeating the same thing again

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone hopelessly out of date, like the extinct bird
second meaning: DO is short for ditto, the same thing

explanation.surface: A fuddy-duddy keeps saying the same thing over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog splits the second half into DO (short for ditto) taken twice; read as one phrase, ditto ditto is simply the same thing said again.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodo is an extinct bird, so the word is used for someone hopelessly behind the times.

clue.text: Extravagant articles about to appear in court case

parts.note: the and a are the definite and indefinite articles

indicators.note: to appear in places the about letter inside the court case word

parts.note: a trial is a case heard in court
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Showy articles are about to be produced in a court case as evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical behaviour is exaggerated and showy, as on a stage, so it matches extravagant.

clue.text: Downpour taking top off sewer

indicators.note: in a down answer the top is the first letter, which is removed from the sewer word

parts.note: a drain is a sewer

explanation.surface: A deluge lifts the cover off a sewer.
explanation.definitionFit: A downpour is a heavy fall of rain, so the word names what falls.

clue.text: Culmination recalled for one enthralled by a US writer

indicators.note: enthralled by says the example word is held inside the writer's name

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the example abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: for one means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A reader recalls being spellbound by an American author.
explanation.definitionFit: The apogee is the highest point of an orbit, hence the peak or climax of anything.

clue.text: Limits to Prince adopting a language with royal attributes

indicators.note: adopting means the outer letters take in the next part
the limits of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of Prince
Latin is a language

explanation.surface: A prince is limited by having to adopt a regal language.
explanation.definitionFit: A count palatine held powers in his territory normally reserved to a sovereign, hence royal privileges.

clue.text: Impulsively hosting King and I with a certain charm

indicators.note: hosting means the impulsive word holds the king letter and I

parts.note: rashly means impulsively, without thinking
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: The King and I is a musical, and someone hosts it on a whim with some charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Rakishly describes the dashing, jaunty manner of a rake, a stylish if disreputable kind of appeal.
